jobs.title: Director Engineering, Systems & Digital
jobs.description:
Lead globally. Transform engineering. Deliver what matters.
At Sedgman, we’re redefining how engineering works at scale.
As Director Engineering, Systems & Digital, you will step into a global leadership role shaping engineering governance, systems and digital capability across Sedgman’s international engineering network.
This newly created role will lead the global optimisation and transformation of engineering delivery. You will establish and embed best practice systems, standards and governance frameworks, while championing integrated digital engineering, data and AI-enabled solutions that improve productivity, quality, decision-making and delivery predictability.
In this role, you will:
- Lead the development and adoption of engineering governance frameworks, systems and standards that enable high-performing engineering delivery globally.
- Provide functional leadership for global engineering systems, standards and governance, establishing scalable frameworks that drive consistency, quality and execution discipline across regions without direct operational ownership of engineering delivery teams.
- Align engineering systems. processes and tools to enable efficient, seamless delivery at scale across complex project environments.
- Champion the adoption of integrated digital engineering, data and AI-enabled capabilities to improve productivity, decision-making and delivery outcomes.
- Establish a consistent global approach to engineering execution that enhances predictability, reduces risk and strengthens delivery performance.
- Use data and performance insights to continuously improve quality, efficiency and overall project outcomes.
- Drive strong commercial outcomes through effective governance of engineering systems, software vendors and strategic investments.
- Partner with regional leadership to align engineering capability with business priorities, growth objectives and long-term performance.

What we’re looking for
You’re a strategic and technically credible engineering leader with the ability to operate globally, influence change at scale and build the systems, standards and capability that enable high-performing engineering project delivery.
- A degree-qualified engineering leader with 20+ years’ experience in engineering design across minerals processing, oil and gas, chemical or related sectors.
- Senior leadership experience across complex, multi-discipline engineering teams.
- Strong EPCM experience, including engineering systems integration and delivery governance.
- Deep understanding of engineering applications, BIM/CDE environments and emerging digital engineering capability.
- Demonstrated experience operating across regions, cultures and matrixed stakeholder groups.
- Commercially astute, outcome-focused and confident translating strategy into execution.
- Innovative, decisive and adaptable, with a continuous improvement mindset.
- A strong communicator who can influence globally and bring teams with you through change.

Why this role?
This is a career-defining opportunity to transform how engineering is delivered globally, with real influence over systems, capability, governance and performance.
If you’re looking for more in your next move, you’ll find it here: more purpose in shaping how global engineering is delivered, more perspective through working across regions and complex projects, more progress through digital innovation, and more impact through measurable performance outcomes.
You’ll be supported by a business that values sustainable performance, wellbeing, flexibility and long-term career development.
If this opportunity resonates with you, we’d love to hear from you. Submit your CV and a brief cover letter outlining your relevant leadership experience and the impact you could bring to this role.
More in reach.

jobs.title: Director, Operations
jobs.description:
This is an exciting time to join our team. As we continue to grow, we are looking for talented professionals who are ready to contribute, collaborate with exceptional colleagues, and help shape the future of the built environment. If you are looking for a place where your expertise will be valued, your career can grow, and your work will make a difference, we invite you to explore what is possible with us.

We empower our employees to choose where they work whether remotely, from home or from one of our office locations because we believe flexibility, trust, and collaboration drive great results.

NORR delivers low-carbon, high-performance commercial and residential environments through a holistic, multidisciplinary approach led by architects, interior designers, and engineers. With experience spanning ground-up developments, repositionings, workplace strategies, coworking spaces, and multi-family residential projects, the firm creates innovative, market-responsive solutions that support business objectives, smart growth, wellness, urban regeneration, and long-term sustainability. Guided by a client-centric methodology, NORR integrates carbon-reduction strategies, resilient infrastructure, and design excellence to deliver lasting value, efficiency, and vibrant communities.

Learn more about our Commercial and Residential Portfolios.

We are looking for an accomplished Director of Operations to lead operational performance and strengthen project delivery across our Commercial and Residential Studios and Practice Areas. In this role, you will translate business priorities into effective operational plans, drive financial and organizational performance, and ensure our teams have the leadership, resources and support needed to succeed. Working in close partnership with the VP, Operations, and sector leadership, you will play an important role in advancing the business and supporting its continued growth and profitability

You Will Make an Impact by

Driving operational and financial performance, supporting business objectives, profitability, and sustainable growth.
Strengthening project delivery, operational standards and accountability across Studios and Practice Areas.
Optimizing resource planning, workforce capacity, and utilization to meet business and project demands.
Developing and supporting Studio Managers and Practice Leaders, building leadership capability and team effectiveness.
Identifying operational challenges and opportunities, implementing improvements that enhance efficiency, quality, and client outcomes.

You will Bring to the Team

A degree in Architecture, Interior Design, Engineering, Construction Management, or a related discipline, with at least 12–15 years of progressive professional experience, including significant operational or senior leadership responsibility.

Experience leading project delivery and operational performance across multiple teams, Studios, or business units.
A collaborative and decisive leadership approach, with the ability to influence, develop others and build accountability.
Sound judgment and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate business priorities into practical results.
Experience in leading or supporting Commercial and Residential Studios would be a strong asset.

We Are

The spaces we design and the technology we embrace shape how people live, work, learn, and connect. As an employee-owned, integrated Architecture and Engineering company, you will collaborate with talented professionals on projects that make a lasting impact on communities across Canada, the US, and the UK.

At NORR we are committed to innovation, advancing sustainable design and helping our clients reduce environmental impact, and shaping a net-zero future. We invest in our employees by fostering continuous learning, encouraging innovative thinking, and creating opportunities to solve complex challenges, grow professionally and build meaningful careers.

jobs.title: Head of Security
jobs.description:
Listed on CyberJobs.cc, a job board for cybersecurity jobs from the team behind AITraining.jobs.

Tonic.ai has been de-identifying sensitive data since 2018, and hundreds of enterprises use our products, among them eBay, UnitedHealth Group, Qualcomm, Commonwealth Bank, and Mercor. Our customers hand us some of the most sensitive data they have: production databases, patient and financial records, and increasingly the email, chat, documents and code that AI labs want to train on.

That makes security part of what we sell, not just how we operate. Every deal runs through a security review, every customer asks how their data is protected, and the AI tools our own team uses every day raise new questions faster than most policies can keep up. We're looking for a Head of Security who can own all of it.

Why This Role, Why Now

Our customers are getting bigger and more regulated, and our products now sit in the middle of AI training-data deals where the buyer, the seller and their lawyers all want proof that the data was handled safely. The bar for our own security program is rising with them. What keeps deals moving is a security leader who can pass the audit, answer the questionnaire, get on the call with a customer's CISO, and keep our own house in order at the same time.

That's this job. You'll be Tonic's senior security leader, working directly with our founders, engineering, DevOps, sales and legal. You'll own the program end to end, setting the strategy and doing much of the hands-on work yourself.

What You'll Do

Own our SOC 2 program end to end: scoping, evidence collection, control remediation, and the auditor relationship.
Keep our practices aligned with GDPR, HIPAA, and the security commitments in our customer contracts.
Partner with engineering to build security into the development lifecycle, from design review through release, so products ship securely and on time.
Run vulnerability management across our code, dependencies, and infrastructure, including pen tests and remediation tracking.
Secure and govern our AWS, GCP, and Azure environments (IAM, configuration, logging, hardening), working closely with DevOps and backend engineers.
Act as the customer-facing security expert. Own security questionnaires and RFP responses, and join sales calls when a customer wants to go deep.
Work with legal on contract negotiations and security redlines.
Run corporate security and IT: endpoint management and laptop hardening, EDR monitoring, and incident response.
Own identity and access management and vendor risk management across the company.
Set and maintain policies and guardrails for employee AI use, including LLM platforms, coding assistants, and MCP connectors, covering access controls, data handling, and vendor review of AI providers.
Keep those AI policies current as the landscape moves, so the team can adopt new tools quickly and safely.

What We're Looking For

Several years leading security at a B2B software company, with a record of building programs rather than inheriting them.
SOC 2 audits owned end to end, plus working knowledge of GDPR and HIPAA.
Hands-on experience securing AWS, GCP, and Azure. You can read an IAM policy, spot a misconfiguration, and fix it with the engineer who owns it.
Experience embedding security in the development lifecycle and running vulnerability management without becoming the team that slows everything down.
Comfort in front of customers. You can answer a 300-question security questionnaire, hold your own on a call with a customer's CISO, and work through redlines with legal.
Experience running corporate security and IT: endpoint management, EDR, incident response, IAM, and vendor risk.
AI-native workflow. You use AI tools yourself, understand where they create real risk, and can write guardrails that people actually follow.
Self-direction. You'll be the security leader, and you'll need to make sound, risk-based calls without waiting for someone to tell you what to do.
Clear communication with very different audiences, from an engineer debugging a finding to an executive weighing a tradeoff.

Nice to Haves

Experience at a data infrastructure, privacy, or AI company.
Experience selling into regulated industries such as healthcare and financial services.
Experience with ISO 27001, HITRUST, or FedRAMP.
Experience securing software that customers deploy in their own environments, alongside SaaS.
Experience at an early-stage or fast-growing company.

What Success Looks Like

In your first month, you'll learn our products, infrastructure, and current controls, take over the security questionnaire queue, and build a clear picture of our biggest risks. By the end of your first quarter, you'll own the SOC 2 program and auditor relationship, have a prioritized roadmap across product, cloud, and corporate security, and have AI-use policies in place that the team actually follows. After that, you'll help shape how security grows at Tonic, including whether and when we hire next.

Why Join

You'll own security at a company where security is part of the product, not a back-office function.
You'll work directly with our founders, with a real say in how the company handles risk and makes commitments to customers.
You'll get close to the AI training-data market and help set the bar for how sensitive data should be handled in it.
You'll shape AI governance in real time, at a company whose own business is making data safe for AI.
Competitive compensation and equity.

Benefits We Offer

Competitive salary and equity
Unlimited paid time off
401k plan with employer contribution
Medical, dental, and vision insurance
Generous parental leave policy
Remote-friendly work environment

Tonic.ai is an equal opportunity employer. We're building a team that reflects the diversity of our users and the problems they're trying to solve.

jobs.title: Head of Finance
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Gastronomous is hiring its first full-time Head of Finance, an executive role spanning finance and operations. You will sit at the executive table, report to the CEO, attend our quarterly board meetings, and build the financial backbone of a robotics company in the middle of a major scale-up.

This role keeps the books, and goes far beyond them. You will be a leader and a champion of our growth: shaping pricing, steering the finances of our operation, raising capital and helping take us into new countries. The role is built to grow into CFO after our Series A.

Head of Finance

Oakville, Ontario (on-site)
Full-time, permanent

About Gastronomous

We are building the “Kitchen of the Future” for quick-service restaurants. We design, engineer and manufacture AI-powered kitchen automation: ChronoGrill™, an autonomous open-flame grill; Ghost, automated beverage pouring; and Gastroverse, our IoT cloud platform that monitors every machine in the field.

How we work.

We are a no-nonsense team of passionate, execution-driven people. Our ability to deliver, not just dream, sets us apart: inside and outside the company, we do what we say we will do. Our people are trusted to act independently, make practical decisions and move fast. We build the future one deployment at a time.

How fast we are growing.

The last 12 to 16 months changed the shape of the company:

Purchase orders signed with major brands, moving us from pilots to rollout
A new office in La Mirada, California to support US deployments; most of our customers are in the US, across many states
Our own ERP, built in-house to run parts, BOMs, inventory, work orders and purchasing

The next 12 to 16 months are bigger: scale across North America, sign new major accounts, enter new markets, secure new financing, and build an organization that can grow quickly and efficiently. We are about 35 people, mostly technical, headquartered in Oakville, Ontario.

Why This Role

A seat at the executive table. You report to the CEO, work directly with our founders, and help set company direction, not just report on it.
In the boardroom. You attend our quarterly board meetings and present the numbers, the plan and the trade-offs to our directors and investors.
Champion our growth. Every new account, market and financing round runs through your numbers. You will see your work show up in deals signed and machines deployed.
Breadth few finance roles offer. Two countries and counting, manufacturing, equipment, service and software revenue, government funding and venture fundraising, all in one seat.
Build it from the ground up. Our finance function, pricing model, financial controls and new-market playbook are yours to design. There is no inherited bureaucracy to work around.
A path to CFO. This role is designed to grow into CFO after the Series A.
A team behind you. You start with a full-time bookkeeper and build the team as the company grows.

What You Will Own

Your work falls into two halves of roughly equal weight. You run an efficient close, so you have real time for the decisions that grow the company.

Lead the finance function

You will set up our systems and processes and do much of the work yourself, making sure every entry, filing and payment is right.

Close and reporting. Lead the month-end close for our Canadian parent and US subsidiary, including consolidation and intercompany reconciliation. Deliver timely financial statements and management reports to leadership and the board.
Year-end. Lead year-end for both our Canadian and US entities: the year-end close, the audit or review engagement, and corporate tax returns, working with our external accountants.
Budget and forecasts. Own the annual budget and rolling forecasts, track performance against plan, and report the metrics leadership and the board run the company on: margins, unit economics and cash runway.
Revenue and billing. Own revenue recognition across equipment, service and software contracts. Set customer payment terms and manage deposits and milestone billing.
Accounts receivable. Own all of A/R across both entities: invoicing, customer credit and collections, so cash comes in on time.
Tax, audit and compliance. Manage Canadian and US compliance, including HST/GST, US sales tax, corporate filings and transfer pricing, working with our external advisors.
Payroll and benefits. Set up and run payroll in Canada and the US, including Records of Employment (ROEs). Administer our employee benefits programs, from enrolments and changes to provider relationships, keeping both accurate, compliant and cost-effective.
SR&ED and government funding. Assist with preparing our SR&ED claims, from tracking eligible costs to filing. Find, apply for, claim and report on grants and funding programs.
Systems and day-to-day accounting. Set up our accounting systems, internal controls and policies. Work hands-on with our bookkeeper on A/P, journal entries, reconciliations and expenses until each process runs cleanly.
Drive the financial side of our operations
Pricing and margins. Evaluate product and service pricing, build landed costing from bills of materials, contract-manufacturer quotes, freight and duties, and track margins.
Inventory and systems. Own inventory accounting and valuation, and keep our in-house ERP and QuickBooks reconciled so every cost and margin can be trusted.
US operations. Own the budget for our US office and work with its team to run it efficiently.
Cash and financing. Manage cash flow, working capital, banking relationships and USD/CAD exposure. Secure external financing, including inventory financing. Support equity fundraising: cap table, data room and financial diligence.
Business cases. Partner with operations, engineering and sales on capital purchases and investment decisions.
Insurance and risk. Manage our insurance program across Canada and the US, including renewals, coverage reviews and the certificates our customers require.
New markets. Build the financial setup for each new market we enter.

Who You Are

You are an operator, not a scorekeeper. Taking on new challenges that matter to the growth of a business is what excites you. You use the numbers to change a price, a budget or a contract. You find a way to deliver without a playbook, and you earn the trust of managers, suppliers, outside advisors and investors.

What You Bring

5+ years of progressive accounting and finance experience
You have owned finance end to end as the senior finance leader, or as the clear #2 who owned the close: monthly close, financial statements, and work with outside auditors and tax advisors
Hands-on: you have set up accounting systems and personally run payroll, A/R, A/P, journal entries and filings, not only reviewed them
A track record of owning finance-related operations beyond accounting, such as pricing, budgets or financing
Strong working knowledge of ASPE and/or IFRS
Advanced Excel and hands-on QuickBooks experience (QuickBooks Online preferred)
You can work on-site, 5 days/week at our Oakville headquarters

What Sets You Apart

CPA designation and a degree in accounting, finance or commerce
Manufacturing, hardware or equipment experience: inventory, standard or product costing, COGS, ERP
Experience in a fast-paced, growth-stage environment
Designing service, maintenance or recurring-revenue models for equipment
Government funding programs such as SR&ED and IRAP
Cross-border Canada/US finance: intercompany, USD/CAD, US GAAP, US sales tax and state filings
Leading people

What We Offer

The chance to make your mark at a fast-paced company
A leadership role with a clear path to CFO
Stock options under our equity incentive plan
Health, dental and vision care
Disability, life and group insurance

Salary: $110,000–$130,000 base, plus bonus and equity opportunities.

Accommodations are available on request for candidates with disabilities throughout the hiring process.

jobs.title: Director, Supply Chain Management
jobs.description:
Ottawa, ON | On-site

Position Overview

The Director of Supply Chain Management shapes and leads the supply chain function at Calian GNSS, making business-level decisions with meaningful operational and financial impact as the business grows. The role owns the multi-year supply chain strategy, including supply continuity and risk, inventory and working capital, supplier strategy, and long-term planning.

Working closely with Product, R&D, Sales, Finance and Operations, the Director aligns supply chain decisions with product and business strategy, and collaborates with the Saskatoon supply chain team on procurement and sourcing. The Director leads a small, high-performing team covering supply chain management, master planning and purchasing, stays hands-on in the decisions that matter most, builds organizational capability and succession plans, and presents to senior leadership.

Responsibilities

Develop and own the multi-year supply chain strategy for GNSS, aligned with GNSS and Defence & Space business objectives, annual business plans, and customer expectations. Bring supply chain constraints, risks, and opportunities into GNSS product and business planning.
Own supply chain performance across the business, using lead time (supplier and end-to-end, including variability) as the primary leading indicator, alongside supply continuity risk, working capital, on-time delivery, supplier quality, and cost reduction. Drive improvement in lead time, cost, and fulfillment, and report results to senior leadership.
Own supply continuity and risk, including shortages, obsolescence, single-source exposure, design-outs, and customer allocation decisions, with contingency plans for supply gaps.
Own inventory strategy and working capital, setting inventory targets (including turns and excess and obsolete inventory) that balance customer service, continuity of supply, and cash impact.
Lead demand and longer-term supply chain planning that links product roadmaps, sales forecasts, and financial plans, and lead supply chain input into new product introductions and make/buy decisions.
Set supplier strategy and make major supplier, manufacturing, logistics, and inventory decisions, including the terms of strategic supplier and logistics agreements. Ensure supplier compliance with Calian’s ethics and supplier standards.
Collaborate with the Saskatoon supply chain department on procurement and sourcing, particularly around suppliers and combined buying power, while retaining accountability for GNSS end-to-end supply chain strategy and continuity of supply.
Attract, recruit, onboard, engage, and retain top supply chain talent. Lead, coach, and develop a small, high-performing team, build bench strength and succession plans, and model Calian’s corporate culture.
Develop, monitor, and authorize the department’s budgets, including material spend, inventory investment, and capital investments in supply chain capability, and support audit requests.
Partner with Product, R&D, Sales, Finance, Operations, and other leaders, participate in executive planning and business reviews, and present to senior leadership.
Maintain compliance with regulatory requirements and ethical standards related to procurement, order fulfillment, and international trade, while operating under ISO 9001:2015.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Business, or related field.
10-15 years of progressive supply chain leadership experience in aerospace, defense, high-tech electronics manufacturing or related industries, in both government and commercial environments.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing multi-year supply chain strategy and presenting to executive leadership.
Experience in demand planning and S&OP, new product introduction, make/buy analysis, and inventory and working capital management.
Experience attracting, recruiting, engaging, and developing small, high-performing teams, building bench strength, and succession planning.
Knowledge of electronics and defense regulatory requirements.
Hands-on proficiency in ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, or equivalent)
Solid knowledge of various manufacturing processes, lean and MES.
Excellent leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills.

Compensation

$130K-$180K + bonus

Vacancy

We have 1 available position.

Perks And Benefits

Competitive, company-paid benefits
Generous time off package
Stock purchase plan
RRSP program
Flexible work hours for eligible roles
Programs to support employee health and well-being

jobs.title: Director of Product Development
jobs.description:
Location: Winnipeg, Manitoba | On-site

About EQ3

EQ3 is a Canadian furniture company headquartered in Winnipeg, creating timeless furniture that brings together thoughtful design, quality materials and enduring value. Our business connects Canadian upholstery manufacturing, retail showrooms, e-commerce, and wholesale, giving our product development team a direct role in shaping our collections and the customer experience.

The opportunity

We are looking for a Director of Product Development to lead product strategy and development across the EQ3 portfolio. Reporting to the President, you will guide products from initial concept through development, launch and lifecycle management.

You will combine design judgment with commercial insight to build a cohesive assortment that delivers quality, comfort and value. Working closely with engineering, manufacturing, procurement, marketing, sales and operations, you will turn customer needs and business priorities into a clear product roadmap that supports profitable growth.

This position is based on-site in Winnipeg, Manitoba.

What You'll Do

Lead product strategy, planning and lifecycle management across the EQ3 portfolio.
Develop and manage the product roadmap, setting priorities, milestones and deliverables for new products and improvements to existing collections.
Translate customer feedback, market research and business insights into clear development briefs and business cases.
Guide decisions on materials, construction and product features, balancing design, quality, comfort, durability, cost and manufacturing feasibility.
Collaborate across departments to coordinate product launches and meet financial and customer satisfaction goals.
Evaluate assortment performance and identify opportunities to strengthen collections, improve margins, reduce unnecessary complexity and improve product availability.
Engage with customers and channel partners to understand product performance and emerging needs.
Present product direction, progress, business cases and risks to the President and other stakeholders.
Lead and develop the product development team, establishing clear expectations and strong working relationships across the business.

What You'll Bring

A master's degree in product leadership, business administration, marketing, finance, economics or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
A proven record of developing and launching successful products, managing product lines and building cohesive product portfolios.
Strong commercial judgment and the ability to translate customer research, market insights and performance data into practical decisions.
Demonstrated leadership skills and the ability to influence and align teams across functions.
Excellent communication, presentation and interpersonal skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
Experience in furniture, home furnishings or related consumer products is an asset, particularly in environments that connect design, materials and manufacturing.

Working at EQ3

Join a collaborative team where thoughtful design and practical problem-solving shape the work. You will have the opportunity to influence our product portfolio and work closely with colleagues across manufacturing and our customer-facing channels.

We Offer

A comprehensive benefits package and support for work-life balance.
Employee discounts, wellness programs and group banking benefits.
Community involvement, employee recognition and activities through the EQ3 Spirit Committee.
Opportunities for professional growth and internal advancement.

button on this posting.

We thank all applicants for their interest. Only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Executive Director, The Clarice Smith Performing Arts Center
jobs.location: Urban agglomeration of Montreal, Quebec, Canada
jobs.description:
APPLICATION DEADLINE

November 13, 2026, for Best Consideration

POSITION

Staff Regular

SALARY RANGE

$235,000-$275,000

The Clarice Overview

The Clarice Smith Performing Arts Center (The Clarice) at the University of Maryland (UMD) is part of the College of Arts and Humanities (ARHU) and is the academic and artistic home of the School of Music (SOM); the School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies (TDPS); the Michelle Smith Performing Arts Library (MSPAL); and The Clarice’s own artistic platform Clarice Presents (CP). At the time of its construction, the 318,000-square-foot facility on 17 acres of land was the largest construction project undertaken by the State of Maryland, and remains one of the most complex projects in recent Maryland state history.

The Clarice opened in 2001 and is named in honor of visual artist and philanthropist Clarice Smith (1933-2021). From its founding, The Clarice was conceived as a “creative village” that brought a robust series of outside artists and performers to campus, supported the academic and performance programs of SOM and TDPS and collaborations with MSPAL, and built bridges between UMD and its surrounding community. The Clarice, through its dynamic outreach programs, manifested UMD’s commitment to meaningfully contribute to those communities through the arts and the encouragement of cultural citizenship. The Clarice continues to strengthen its role as the central home for performing arts at UMD, supporting the academic and performance needs of SOM and TDPS, ensuring the excellence and social relevance of all of its programs, and enhancing its leadership position in the field despite the political and financial headwinds for the arts in this country.

The Clarice hosts more than 1,000 public performances and events each year, the majority featuring the artistry of SOM and TDPS students and faculty. The Clarice’s artistic platform, Clarice Presents (CP), offers uniquely integrated performances, digital, civic and community engagement programming. MSPAL, often in partnership with CP and M‐NCPPC, also presents events at The Clarice. All presentations and events are supported by the administrative, production management, and technical staff of The Clarice.

Professional staff across artistic planning, operations, and finance report to the Executive Director, who works in close collaboration with College senior leadership, academic partners, and marketing, communication, and development staff.

Position Summary/Purpose

Reporting directly to the Dean of the College of Arts and Humanities, the Executive Director is ultimately responsible for the management of The Clarice’s staff, operations, facilities, budget, and fundraising. In these roles, the position balances educational, public, and financial priorities to ensure that operations and programming simultaneously enhance The Clarice’s stature as a national leader among performing arts presenters and contribute meaningfully to the resident academic units’ missions; reflect the values of collaboration, belonging, and community; and align with the goals of the college and institution. In collaboration with the Directors of the resident academic units, the position is responsible for the Clarice’s artistic programming and works to ensure that this programming and other initiatives respond to curricular needs. The Executive Director works alongside Directors of the School of Music; the School of Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies; and the Michelle Smith Performing Arts Library, as well as the Executive Director of Arts for All to develop and refine a strategic and innovative vision that enhances the curricular experience for faculty and students, engages the campus, connects with the community, and further enhances the reputation of the University of Maryland. The Executive Director should bring significant knowledge of the changing performing arts landscape and a fierce dedication to collaborative leadership models. The Executive Director meets monthly with the Dean and annually with the Provost and Dean to ensure that the performing arts have a campus and community-wide agenda and impact. For more detailed information about The Clarice please visit this website.

Minimum Qualifications

Education: Bachelor’s degree from accredited college or University.
Experience: Twelve (12) years of professional experience, including at least six (6) years supervising or managing professional staff.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage and inspire stakeholders at all levels.
Ability to make sound decisions, solve complex problems, and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Knowledge of relevant industry regulations and best practices.

Apply

Required application materials: Resume, Cover Letter, List of References

Learn more about UMD, The Clarice and campus partners.

Secure and govern our AWS, GCP, and Azure environments (IAM, configuration, logging, hardening), working closely with DevOps and backend engineers.
Act as the customer-facing security expert. Own security questionnaires and RFP responses, and join sales calls when a customer wants to go deep.
Work with legal on contract negotiations and security redlines.
Run corporate security and IT: endpoint management and laptop hardening, EDR monitoring, and incident response.
Own identity and access management and vendor risk management across the company.
Set and maintain policies and guardrails for employee AI use, including LLM platforms, coding assistants, and MCP connectors, covering access controls, data handling, and vendor review of AI providers.
Keep those AI policies current as the landscape moves, so the team can adopt new tools quickly and safely.

What We're Looking For

Several years leading security at a B2B software company, with a record of building programs rather than inheriting them.
SOC 2 audits owned end to end, plus working knowledge of GDPR and HIPAA.
Hands-on experience securing AWS, GCP, and Azure. You can read an IAM policy, spot a misconfiguration, and fix it with the engineer who owns it.
Experience embedding security in the development lifecycle and running vulnerability management without becoming the team that slows everything down.
Comfort in front of customers. You can answer a 300-question security questionnaire, hold your own on a call with a customer's CISO, and work through redlines with legal.
Experience running corporate security and IT: endpoint management, EDR, incident response, IAM, and vendor risk.
AI-native workflow. You use AI tools yourself, understand where they create real risk, and can write guardrails that people actually follow.
Self-direction. You'll be the security leader, and you'll need to make sound, risk-based calls without waiting for someone to tell you what to do.
Clear communication with very different audiences, from an engineer debugging a finding to an executive weighing a tradeoff.

Nice to Haves

Experience at a data infrastructure, privacy, or AI company.
Experience selling into regulated industries such as healthcare and financial services.
Experience with ISO 27001, HITRUST, or FedRAMP.
Experience securing software that customers deploy in their own environments, alongside SaaS.
Experience at an early-stage or fast-growing company.

What Success Looks Like

In your first month, you'll learn our products, infrastructure, and current controls, take over the security questionnaire queue, and build a clear picture of our biggest risks. By the end of your first quarter, you'll own the SOC 2 program and auditor relationship, have a prioritized roadmap across product, cloud, and corporate security, and have AI-use policies in place that the team actually follows. After that, you'll help shape how security grows at Tonic, including whether and when we hire next.

Why Join

You'll own security at a company where security is part of the product, not a back-office function.
You'll work directly with our founders, with a real say in how the company handles risk and makes commitments to customers.
You'll get close to the AI training-data market and help set the bar for how sensitive data should be handled in it.
You'll shape AI governance in real time, at a company whose own business is making data safe for AI.
Competitive compensation and equity.

Benefits We Offer

Competitive salary and equity

401k plan with employer contribution
Medical, dental, and vision insurance
Generous parental leave policy
Remote-friendly work environment

Tonic.ai is an equal opportunity employer. We're building a team that reflects the diversity of our users and the problems they're trying to solve.

new_jobs.title: Head of Finance
new_jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Gastronomous is hiring its first full-time Head of Finance, an executive role spanning finance and operations. You will sit at the executive table, report to the CEO, attend our quarterly board meetings, and build the financial backbone of a robotics company in the middle of a major scale-up.

This role keeps the books, and goes far beyond them. You will be a leader and a champion of our growth: shaping pricing, steering the finances of our operation, raising capital and helping take us into new countries. The role is built to grow into CFO after our Series A.

Head of Finance

Oakville, Ontario (on-site)
Full-time, permanent

About Gastronomous

We are building the “Kitchen of the Future” for quick-service restaurants. We design, engineer and manufacture AI-powered kitchen automation: ChronoGrill™, an autonomous open-flame grill; Ghost, automated beverage pouring; and Gastroverse, our IoT cloud platform that monitors every machine in the field.

How we work.

We are a no-nonsense team of passionate, execution-driven people. Our ability to deliver, not just dream, sets us apart: inside and outside the company, we do what we say we will do. Our people are trusted to act independently, make practical decisions and move fast. We build the future one deployment at a time.

How fast we are growing.

The last 12 to 16 months changed the shape of the company:

Purchase orders signed with major brands, moving us from pilots to rollout
A new office in La Mirada, California to support US deployments; most of our customers are in the US, across many states
Our own ERP, built in-house to run parts, BOMs, inventory, work orders and purchasing

The next 12 to 16 months are bigger: scale across North America, sign new major accounts, enter new markets, secure new financing, and build an organization that can grow quickly and efficiently. We are about 35 people, mostly technical, headquartered in Oakville, Ontario.

Why This Role

A seat at the executive table. You report to the CEO, work directly with our founders, and help set company direction, not just report on it.
In the boardroom. You attend our quarterly board meetings and present the numbers, the plan and the trade-offs to our directors and investors.
Champion our growth. Every new account, market and financing round runs through your numbers. You will see your work show up in deals signed and machines deployed.
Breadth few finance roles offer. Two countries and counting, manufacturing, equipment, service and software revenue, government funding and venture fundraising, all in one seat.
Build it from the ground up. Our finance function, pricing model, financial controls and new-market playbook are yours to design. There is no inherited bureaucracy to work around.
A path to CFO. This role is designed to grow into CFO after the Series A.
A team behind you. You start with a full-time bookkeeper and build the team as the company grows.

What You Will Own

Your work falls into two halves of roughly equal weight. You run an efficient close, so you have real time for the decisions that grow the company.

Lead the finance function

You will set up our systems and processes and do much of the work yourself, making sure every entry, filing and payment is right.

Close and reporting. Lead the month-end close for our Canadian parent and US subsidiary, including consolidation and intercompany reconciliation. Deliver timely financial statements and management reports to leadership and the board.
Year-end. Lead year-end for both our Canadian and US entities: the year-end close, the audit or review engagement, and corporate tax returns, working with our external accountants.
Budget and forecasts. Own the annual budget and rolling forecasts, track performance against plan, and report the metrics leadership and the board run the company on: margins, unit economics and cash runway.
Revenue and billing. Own revenue recognition across equipment, service and software contracts. Set customer payment terms and manage deposits and milestone billing.
Accounts receivable. Own all of A/R across both entities: invoicing, customer credit and collections, so cash comes in on time.
Tax, audit and compliance. Manage Canadian and US compliance, including HST/GST, US sales tax, corporate filings and transfer pricing, working with our external advisors.
Payroll and benefits. Set up and run payroll in Canada and the US, including Records of Employment (ROEs). Administer our employee benefits programs, from enrolments and changes to provider relationships, keeping both accurate, compliant and cost-effective.
SR&ED and government funding. Assist with preparing our SR&ED claims, from tracking eligible costs to filing. Find, apply for, claim and report on grants and funding programs.
Systems and day-to-day accounting. Set up our accounting systems, internal controls and policies. Work hands-on with our bookkeeper on A/P, journal entries, reconciliations and expenses until each process runs cleanly.
Drive the financial side of our operations
Pricing and margins. Evaluate product and service pricing, build landed costing from bills of materials, contract-manufacturer quotes, freight and duties, and track margins.
Inventory and systems. Own inventory accounting and valuation, and keep our in-house ERP and QuickBooks reconciled so every cost and margin can be trusted.
US operations. Own the budget for our US office and work with its team to run it efficiently.
Cash and financing. Manage cash flow, working capital, banking relationships and USD/CAD exposure. Secure external financing, including inventory financing. Support equity fundraising: cap table, data room and financial diligence.
Business cases. Partner with operations, engineering and sales on capital purchases and investment decisions.
Insurance and risk. Manage our insurance program across Canada and the US, including renewals, coverage reviews and the certificates our customers require.
New markets. Build the financial setup for each new market we enter.

Who You Are

You are an operator, not a scorekeeper. Taking on new challenges that matter to the growth of a business is what excites you. You use the numbers to change a price, a budget or a contract. You find a way to deliver without a playbook, and you earn the trust of managers, suppliers, outside advisors and investors.

What You Bring

5+ years of progressive accounting and finance experience
You have owned finance end to end as the senior finance leader, or as the clear #2 who owned the close: monthly close, financial statements, and work with outside auditors and tax advisors
Hands-on: you have set up accounting systems and personally run payroll, A/R, A/P, journal entries and filings, not only reviewed them
A track record of owning finance-related operations beyond accounting, such as pricing, budgets or financing
Strong working knowledge of ASPE and/or IFRS
Advanced Excel and hands-on QuickBooks experience (QuickBooks Online preferred)
You can work on-site, 5 days/week at our Oakville headquarters

What Sets You Apart

CPA designation and a degree in accounting, finance or commerce
Manufacturing, hardware or equipment experience: inventory, standard or product costing, COGS, ERP
Experience in a fast-paced, growth-stage environment
Designing service, maintenance or recurring-revenue models for equipment
Government funding programs such as SR&ED and IRAP
Cross-border Canada/US finance: intercompany, USD/CAD, US GAAP, US sales tax and state filings
Leading people

What We Offer

The chance to make your mark at a fast-paced company
A leadership role with a clear path to CFO
Stock options under our equity incentive plan
Health, dental and vision care
Disability, life and group insurance

Salary: $110,000–$130,000 base, plus bonus and equity opportunities.

Accommodations are available on request for candidates with disabilities throughout the hiring process.

new_jobs.description:
Ottawa, ON | On-site

Position Overview

The Director of Supply Chain Management shapes and leads the supply chain function at Calian GNSS, making business-level decisions with meaningful operational and financial impact as the business grows. The role owns the multi-year supply chain strategy, including supply continuity and risk, inventory and working capital, supplier strategy, and long-term planning.

Working closely with Product, R&D, Sales, Finance and Operations, the Director aligns supply chain decisions with product and business strategy, and collaborates with the Saskatoon supply chain team on procurement and sourcing. The Director leads a small, high-performing team covering supply chain management, master planning and purchasing, stays hands-on in the decisions that matter most, builds organizational capability and succession plans, and presents to senior leadership.

Responsibilities

Develop and own the multi-year supply chain strategy for GNSS, aligned with GNSS and Defence & Space business objectives, annual business plans, and customer expectations. Bring supply chain constraints, risks, and opportunities into GNSS product and business planning.
Own supply chain performance across the business, using lead time (supplier and end-to-end, including variability) as the primary leading indicator, alongside supply continuity risk, working capital, on-time delivery, supplier quality, and cost reduction. Drive improvement in lead time, cost, and fulfillment, and report results to senior leadership.
Own supply continuity and risk, including shortages, obsolescence, single-source exposure, design-outs, and customer allocation decisions, with contingency plans for supply gaps.
Own inventory strategy and working capital, setting inventory targets (including turns and excess and obsolete inventory) that balance customer service, continuity of supply, and cash impact.
Lead demand and longer-term supply chain planning that links product roadmaps, sales forecasts, and financial plans, and lead supply chain input into new product introductions and make/buy decisions.
Set supplier strategy and make major supplier, manufacturing, logistics, and inventory decisions, including the terms of strategic supplier and logistics agreements. Ensure supplier compliance with Calian’s ethics and supplier standards.
Collaborate with the Saskatoon supply chain department on procurement and sourcing, particularly around suppliers and combined buying power, while retaining accountability for GNSS end-to-end supply chain strategy and continuity of supply.
Attract, recruit, onboard, engage, and retain top supply chain talent. Lead, coach, and develop a small, high-performing team, build bench strength and succession plans, and model Calian’s corporate culture.
Develop, monitor, and authorize the department’s budgets, including material spend, inventory investment, and capital investments in supply chain capability, and support audit requests.
Partner with Product, R&D, Sales, Finance, Operations, and other leaders, participate in executive planning and business reviews, and present to senior leadership.
Maintain compliance with regulatory requirements and ethical standards related to procurement, order fulfillment, and international trade, while operating under ISO 9001:2015.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Business, or related field.
10-15 years of progressive supply chain leadership experience in aerospace, defense, high-tech electronics manufacturing or related industries, in both government and commercial environments.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing multi-year supply chain strategy and presenting to executive leadership.
Experience in demand planning and S&OP, new product introduction, make/buy analysis, and inventory and working capital management.
Experience attracting, recruiting, engaging, and developing small, high-performing teams, building bench strength, and succession planning.
Knowledge of electronics and defense regulatory requirements.
Hands-on proficiency in ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, or equivalent)
Solid knowledge of various manufacturing processes, lean and MES.
Excellent leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills.

Compensation

$130K-$180K + bonus

Vacancy

We have 1 available position.

Competitive, company-paid benefits
Generous time off package
Stock purchase plan
RRSP program
Flexible work hours for eligible roles
Programs to support employee health and well-being

new_jobs.title: Director of Product Development
new_jobs.description:
Location: Winnipeg, Manitoba | On-site

About EQ3

EQ3 is a Canadian furniture company headquartered in Winnipeg, creating timeless furniture that brings together thoughtful design, quality materials and enduring value. Our business connects Canadian upholstery manufacturing, retail showrooms, e-commerce, and wholesale, giving our product development team a direct role in shaping our collections and the customer experience.

The opportunity

We are looking for a Director of Product Development to lead product strategy and development across the EQ3 portfolio. Reporting to the President, you will guide products from initial concept through development, launch and lifecycle management.

You will combine design judgment with commercial insight to build a cohesive assortment that delivers quality, comfort and value. Working closely with engineering, manufacturing, procurement, marketing, sales and operations, you will turn customer needs and business priorities into a clear product roadmap that supports profitable growth.

This position is based on-site in Winnipeg, Manitoba.

What You'll Do

Lead product strategy, planning and lifecycle management across the EQ3 portfolio.
Develop and manage the product roadmap, setting priorities, milestones and deliverables for new products and improvements to existing collections.
Translate customer feedback, market research and business insights into clear development briefs and business cases.
Guide decisions on materials, construction and product features, balancing design, quality, comfort, durability, cost and manufacturing feasibility.
Collaborate across departments to coordinate product launches and meet financial and customer satisfaction goals.
Evaluate assortment performance and identify opportunities to strengthen collections, improve margins, reduce unnecessary complexity and improve product availability.
Engage with customers and channel partners to understand product performance and emerging needs.
Present product direction, progress, business cases and risks to the President and other stakeholders.
Lead and develop the product development team, establishing clear expectations and strong working relationships across the business.

What You'll Bring

A master's degree in product leadership, business administration, marketing, finance, economics or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
A proven record of developing and launching successful products, managing product lines and building cohesive product portfolios.
Strong commercial judgment and the ability to translate customer research, market insights and performance data into practical decisions.
Demonstrated leadership skills and the ability to influence and align teams across functions.
Excellent communication, presentation and interpersonal skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
Experience in furniture, home furnishings or related consumer products is an asset, particularly in environments that connect design, materials and manufacturing.

Working at EQ3

Join a collaborative team where thoughtful design and practical problem-solving shape the work. You will have the opportunity to influence our product portfolio and work closely with colleagues across manufacturing and our customer-facing channels.

We Offer

A comprehensive benefits package and support for work-life balance.
Employee discounts, wellness programs and group banking benefits.
Community involvement, employee recognition and activities through the EQ3 Spirit Committee.
Opportunities for professional growth and internal advancement.

Submit your résumé and cover letter using the Apply

button on this posting.

We thank all applicants for their interest. Only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.
